system_description.narrative_title: Drone-led escalation widens Russia–Ukraine war with regional spillovers
system_description.narrative_summary: A surge in drone and missile strikes is extending the Russia–Ukraine war beyond front lines — targeting energy infrastructure, commercial assets and maritime traffic — while provoking cross-border incidents, domestic political upheaval in Kyiv, and strains on international sanctions and supply chains. As an open system this dynamic consists of flows of kinetic attacks, retaliatory strikes, information, political legitimacy, arms transfers and economic impacts; inputs (foreign support, weapons, sanctions, protests) produce outputs (infrastructure damage, fuel shortages, leadership changes, diplomatic friction) that feed back to change tactics, alliances and economic behaviour. The system links military operations, state and corporate actors, and regional air/maritime security, producing reinforcing cycles (attacks → economic pain → alternative sourcing → political pressure) and balancing attempts (diplomatic talks, sanctions, defence production cooperation).
system_description.scope: Inside: military operations (drones, missiles, naval strikes), Ukrainian political leadership and protests, Russian domestic impacts and retaliations, regional airspace and maritime incidents (e.g., Romania, Caspian Sea), sanctions and trade responses, defence-industrial cooperation (drone production, missile defence), and immediate humanitarian and infrastructure consequences (energy, retail, transport).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical and economic order (international security architecture, energy and trade networks, sanctions regime).
adjacent_subsystems: Defense-industrial complex and arms markets (drone production/manufacturing)
Regional security of neighbouring states (NATO frontier and Caspian/Black Sea states)
International sanctions/diplomatic institutions (EU, UN, bilateral diplomacy)

variables.name: Kinetic attack rate
variables.description: The tempo and intensity of offensive kinetic actions (drones, missiles, naval strikes) across the theatre.

variables.name: Retaliatory strike rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of counter‑strikes and reciprocal military actions in response to attacks.

variables.name: Infrastructure damage level
variables.description: The current cumulative physical damage to critical infrastructure such as energy, transport and industrial assets.

variables.name: Energy supply shortfall
variables.description: The deficit between energy demand and available or deliverable energy supplies in affected regions.

variables.name: Commercial asset risk
variables.description: The perceived vulnerability and expected loss probability for commercial and retail assets from conflict and related disruptions.

variables.name: Cross‑border incident rate
variables.description: The rate of incursions, shootdowns, seizures or other air/sea/land incidents that cross or threaten international boundaries.

variables.name: Civilian casualty rate
variables.description: The rate of civilian fatalities and injuries resulting from military operations and spillover incidents.

variables.name: Political legitimacy level
variables.description: The level of public support, trust and perceived legitimacy enjoyed by national political leadership.

variables.name: Protest activity level
variables.description: The intensity, frequency and geographic spread of public protests, demonstrations and civil unrest.

variables.name: Defence production capacity
variables.description: The available manufacturing and logistical capacity to produce and sustain weapons, drones and defensive systems.

variables.name: Arms transfer flow
variables.description: The volume, tempo and reliability of external weapons, munitions and military assistance deliveries into the system.

variables.name: Sanction pressure level
variables.description: The intensity, breadth and economic weight of sanctions, export controls and financial restrictions applied to actors in the conflict.

variables.name: Supply chain disruption
variables.description: The extent and persistence of interruptions to trade routes, logistics networks and commodity flows affecting economic activity.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement
variables.description: The level and intensity of formal diplomatic activity, negotiation, mediation and interstate communication related to the conflict.

variables.name: Economic pain level
variables.description: The aggregate economic hardship experienced by populations and firms, manifest in price spikes, shortages and income loss.

variables.name: Information signal volume
variables.description: The volume, velocity and saturation of information flows including media coverage, announcements and disinformation.

catalysts.title: US–Ukraine joint drone production ramp-up
catalysts.description: Planned US–Ukraine joint drone production and US manufacturing of drone boats will expand matériel output and transfer capacity.
catalysts.rationale: Zelenskiy: US, Ukraine moving forward on joint drone production; US to make Ukrainian drone boats.

catalysts.title: Continued drone airspace breaches into Romania
catalysts.description: Multiple drone incursions and shootdowns in Romanian airspace are likely to recur, raising NATO border incident risks and diplomatic friction.
catalysts.rationale: Romania shot down second and third drones; president calls breaches 'intolerable' (multiple headlines).

catalysts.title: Risk of Iranian retaliation after Caspian Sea strikes
catalysts.description: Iran's statements that attacks 'cannot go unanswered' after Ukrainian strikes on Iranian-linked vessels raise the risk of Iranian reprisals or proxy actions.
catalysts.rationale: Iran: Ukraine's attack on vessel in Caspian 'cannot go unanswered'; Ukraine struck Iranian vessels (headlines).

catalysts.title: European missile-defence prototype target (by mid-2027)
catalysts.description: Europe's target to deliver a prototype European missile-defence system by mid‑2027 will accelerate defence production and allied cooperation if met.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: Ukraine wants prototype of European missile defence system by mid-2027.

catalysts.title: Fragmentation of new EU Russia-sanctions push
catalysts.description: Political resistance within Europe to new Russia sanctions may reduce sanction pressure while prompting intensified diplomatic activity to salvage consensus.
catalysts.rationale: EU faces crumbling support for new Russia sanctions; China expands export-control list (headlines).

catalysts.title: Ongoing Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure
catalysts.description: Repeated drone and missile attacks on Russian refineries and fuel infrastructure will raise infrastructure damage and fuel shortfalls, forcing imports and disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Ukrainian strikes hit Tyumen oil refinery; strikes damaged refineries, Russia importing fuel.

catalysts.title: Escalating Ukrainian political crisis and protests
catalysts.description: Ministerial sackings, replacement of top generals and mass protests indicate sustained domestic political turmoil that may undermine legitimacy and defence organization.
catalysts.rationale: Zelenskiy sacks defence minister; replaces top general after mass protests; protests swell (headlines).

catalysts.title: Campaign targeting commercial assets (Wildberries etc.)
catalysts.description: Continued strikes on high-profile commercial targets and warehouses will raise commercial risk perceptions and information saturation domestically and abroad.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Wildberries warehouses hit by Ukrainian drones; attacks 'bring war home' to middle class.

catalysts.title: Reported US–Ukraine air ceasefire talks
catalysts.description: Reports of US–Ukraine discussions on an air ceasefire could reduce aerial strikes if formalized, but are currently uncertain and contested by Moscow.
catalysts.rationale: Kremlin says too early to comment on reported US–Ukraine air ceasefire talks (headline).
